extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting research articles to the journal Algebraic & Geometric Topology (AGT)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting a research manuscript to the journal Algebraic & Geometric Topology, including ethical rules, formatting, required items (abstract, keywords, authors, references, figures), and production steps after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical guidelines (intellectual property, plagiarism, contributorship, disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to meet our ethical guidelines on intellectual property, plagiarism, contributorship, and disclosure of financial support. See the full policies for authors here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must follow the journal's full policies on authorship and disclosures (link provided). This implies proper attribution, no plagiarism, transparent contributorship, and disclosure of funding/conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / simultaneous_submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript acknowledges that the manuscript is original and is not, in whole or in part, published or under consideration for publication elsewhere. Authors are also required to attest that the manuscript will not be submitted elsewhere while under consideration for publication in this journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submitted article must not be a revision of a rejected article previously submitted to this journal, unless the authors have been explicitly invited to resubmit by the editorial board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of papers submitted to this journal may use AI tools for light editing, such as spell-checking and help with grammar, without acknowledgment. Any use of AI in aid of the arguments in a paper or the citations in a paper must be acknowledged. Papers largely created by AI may not be submitted to this journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge AI when it materially contributes to the argumentation or citation content; trivial grammar/spell-checking tools need not be acknowledged. Do not submit papers largely created by AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of editor suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: During submission, authors will be asked to suggest one or more suitable editors to initially handle their submission. They should choose the editor whose interests are closest to the subject of the paper, but who is not directly connected to one of the authors (e.g., as a former advisor/student, a close relative, a colleague at the same institution, or a close collaborator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest editors with matching subject interests and no close personal/professional ties to any author. Note that the manuscript may be reassigned to another editor after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles in AGT are usually in English, but articles written in other languages will be considered, provided a relevant editor is comfortable with the language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the article is not in English, two versions of the abstract must be included: one in the language of the article and one in English (see Abstract requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format (PDF upload required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission requires uploading the paper in PDF format here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At submission stage upload a PDF. If your submission is accepted you will then need to supply source files, preferably in a variety of TeX or LaTeX, or in other software such as Word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source files after acceptance / acceptable source formats
rubrics_metrics.description: If your submission is accepted you will then need to supply source files, preferably in a variety of TeX or LaTeX, or in other software such as Word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide source files after acceptance to facilitate production (TeX/LaTeX preferred).

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX instructions and class-file guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Please follow our LaTeX instructions for authors. Please do not use the public class file gtpart.cls, which is out of date. Use whichever class file you prefer (article.cls, amsart.cls, etc.), and we will convert this in production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow the journal's LaTeX instructions and avoid gtpart.cls. Any common class (article.cls, amsart.cls) is acceptable because the production team will convert files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief abstract of about 150 words or fewer must be included. It should be self-contained and not make any reference to the bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the article is not in English, two versions of the abstract must be included, one in the language of the article and one in English. Keep abstracts ≈150 words and self-contained (no bibliographic references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords and Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) code(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords and at least one Mathematics Subject Classification code for the article are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide suitable keywords and at least one MSC code to help classify the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author information requirements (postal address, affiliation, unique email)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each coauthor, postal address and affiliation (if appropriate) are required. Each coauthor must provide a valid email address that belongs only to that person and is not shared with anyone. Changes in email address should be communicated promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete contact details for all coauthors including unique personal emails and postal addresses; update emails promptly if they change.

rubrics_metrics.name: References completeness and attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographical references should be complete, including article titles and page ranges. All references in the bibliography should be cited in the text. The use of BibTeX is preferred but not required. Tags will be converted to the journal format. Authors attest that all documents listed in the bibliography have been read and absorbed by at least one author. Their relevance to the submission should be highlighted by a description explicit enough to orient the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full bibliographic details (titles, page ranges). Cite every bibliography entry in the text. Prefer BibTeX for convenience. At least one author must have read each cited document and explain relevance in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure quality and file-format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures must be of publication quality. After acceptance, you will need to submit the original source files in vector graphics format for all diagrams in your manuscript; vector EPS or vector PDF files are the most useful. Bundle your figure files into a single archive (using zip, tar, rar or other format of your choice) and upload on the link you will be provided at acceptance time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide publication-quality figures; supply original vector source files (EPS or PDF) after acceptance and bundle them into a single archive. For questions, contact graphics@msp.org and give details about how graphics were generated. Each figure should be captioned and numbered so that it can float; small figures can be kept in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint / arXiv policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If your paper has previously been deposited on arXiv, we will need its arXiv number at acceptance time. This allows us to deposit the DOI of the published version on the paper's arXiv page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, provide the arXiv identifier at acceptance so the publisher can link the DOI to the arXiv record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs and production deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Page proofs will be made available to authors (or to the designated corresponding author) in PDF format. Failure to acknowledge the receipt of proofs or to return corrections within the requested deadline may cause publication to be postponed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors (or corresponding author) must promptly acknowledge receipt of proofs and return corrections within the deadline to avoid delays in publication.
